title: A simple flavour needs no complete clarity

captions.physics: Choosing pleasure through a vague impression
captions.energy: Delaying for a more suitable perspective

meaning: Shared leisure can feel rich when uncertain choice and waiting for readiness leave room for a simple pleasure already available to both.
text: Complete clarity about desire does not always precede enjoyment. The Moon in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes seeking through a vague impression: choosing, doubting and looking again. The Hanged Man in energy leans towards delaying until a suitable moment or perspective. The Empress in emotions allows richness in what is available. A simple flavour can contain it. Both need no single correct form beforehand for a small trial to gain free participation and become actual pleasure, beyond another promise for the future.

For example, you debate what to prepare for a quiet evening. Recipes change while fresh bread and jam already sit on the table. **Rich enjoyment can begin with a simple available flavour.** You can taste together and hear what each likes. Preparation needs no grand dish. A little tea already offers conversation, flavour and fullness while the initial idea remains uncertain and a richer programme is still undecided.

The difficulty is considering a simple beginning premature. You await precise desire and prepare better while leaving the present without participation. A pause becomes avoiding choice. Another perspective helps when restoring a concrete trial. Fullness needs no prepared name or complete script. It can arise through experience allowed to happen today without guaranteeing finally suitable conditions or permanently unchanged wishes from both.
